domain.name: Marketing, Content & Growth
domain.description: Practical audience strategy, positioning, content systems, campaigns, channel planning, measurement, and growth experiments.

competencies.name: Audience Research
competencies.description: Understand who the offer is for, what they care about, and how they describe the problem.
competencies.purpose: Ground marketing decisions in customer reality instead of assumptions.

units.title: Audience research starts with behavior
units.content: Useful audience research looks for actual problems, triggers, alternatives, objections, language, and buying context rather than only demographic labels.

units.title: Build an audience insight brief
units.content: Collect customer conversations, support questions, reviews, search language, sales notes, and observed behavior; cluster recurring needs; separate evidence from assumptions; then summarize jobs, pains, desired outcomes, objections, and proof requirements.

units.title: Audience research failures
units.content: Avoid inventing personas from stereotypes, treating one loud customer as the market, confusing stated preference with behavior, and collecting data without connecting it to a decision.

drills.title: Build a service audience brief
drills.prompt: Create an audience insight brief for a local creative service using customer questions, buying triggers, objections, desired outcomes, and evidence gaps.

competencies.name: Positioning & Messaging
competencies.description: Clarify who the offer serves, why it matters, and why it is meaningfully different.
competencies.purpose: Make the market understand the value quickly and accurately.

units.title: Positioning is a choice about relevance
units.content: Strong positioning connects a specific audience, problem, promise, proof, and alternative. It is not a list of every capability.

units.title: Positioning statement workflow
units.content: Define target user, urgent problem, current alternative, desired outcome, differentiator, and proof; write a plain-language statement; test whether a new viewer can explain what the offer is and why it matters.

units.title: Positioning failures
units.content: Avoid generic claims like high quality or innovative, trying to appeal equally to everyone, leading with internal features instead of outcomes, and claiming differentiation without proof.

drills.title: Reposition a crowded service
drills.prompt: A local media service sounds identical to competitors. Rewrite the positioning around a specific customer, urgent outcome, differentiated process, and credible proof.

competencies.name: Content Strategy
competencies.description: Build a repeatable system of content that serves audience needs and business goals.
competencies.purpose: Move from random posting to intentional content with measurable roles.

units.title: Every content piece needs a job
units.content: Content can attract, educate, prove, convert, onboard, retain, or reactivate. A useful system balances these roles instead of asking every post to do everything.

units.title: Content pillar planning
units.content: Define audience problems and business goals; create a small set of content pillars; map formats and channels; assign each idea a funnel role; establish production cadence; then review performance by objective rather than vanity metrics alone.

units.title: Content strategy failures
units.content: Avoid trend chasing with no brand fit, posting without a conversion path, repeating one format until fatigue, and judging educational content only by immediate sales.

drills.title: Build a 30-day content system
drills.prompt: Design a 30-day content plan for a service brand using attraction, education, proof, offer, and retention content across two channels.

competencies.name: Marketing Copywriting
competencies.description: Write clear persuasive copy that connects customer problems, outcomes, proof, and action.
competencies.purpose: Increase understanding and response without hype or deception.

units.title: Problem-outcome-proof copy flow
units.content: Lead with a relevant problem or desired outcome; show why it matters; present the offer as a path; support claims with proof; address key objections; then state one clear next action.

units.title: Specific beats impressive
units.content: Concrete outcomes, constraints, timelines, and proof usually persuade better than adjectives such as premium, revolutionary, or unmatched.

units.title: Copy failures
units.content: Avoid vague headlines, multiple competing calls-to-action, unsupported guarantees, jargon, buried pricing/process expectations, and copy that creates curiosity but not understanding.

drills.title: Write a service landing page outline
drills.prompt: Create a landing-page copy structure for a service with headline, proof, process, objections, offer, and one primary CTA.

competencies.name: Social Platform Strategy
competencies.description: Match content, format, cadence, and interaction to the role of each social platform.
competencies.purpose: Use platforms intentionally instead of cross-posting blindly.

units.title: Channels have different jobs
units.content: A platform may be best for discovery, trust, depth, community, direct response, or retention. The same brand can use different content behaviors without changing its core identity.

units.title: Platform role map
units.content: Choose the audience and business goal; identify where discovery and trust happen; assign each platform a role; adapt hooks, length, format, and CTA; reuse underlying ideas while respecting native behavior.

units.title: Platform strategy failures
units.content: Avoid using every platform the same way, copying trends with no audience fit, over-optimizing for reach with no downstream action, and changing brand voice so much that recognition disappears.

drills.title: Design a two-platform content strategy
drills.prompt: Choose distinct roles for a short-form discovery platform and a long-form trust platform for the same business, including formats, CTA, cadence, and reuse rules.

competencies.name: Campaign Planning
competencies.description: Plan coordinated marketing activity around an offer, launch, event, or objective.
competencies.purpose: Align audience, message, channels, assets, timing, and measurement.

units.title: Campaign brief
units.content: Define objective, audience, offer, key message, proof, channels, assets, timeline, budget, owner, conversion path, and success metric before production begins.

units.title: One campaign, one dominant objective
units.content: A campaign can produce secondary benefits, but the main objective should determine the CTA, measurement, and creative emphasis.

units.title: Campaign failures
units.content: Avoid launching before the conversion path is ready, changing the offer mid-campaign without tracking it, measuring only impressions, and producing assets without distribution ownership.

drills.title: Plan a service launch campaign
drills.prompt: Build a two-week campaign brief for a new premium service, including audience, message, proof, assets, distribution, CTA, and success criteria.

competencies.name: Marketing Analytics
competencies.description: Measure whether marketing activity creates qualified attention, leads, conversions, and profitable outcomes.
competencies.purpose: Improve decisions using business-relevant evidence instead of vanity metrics.

units.title: Metrics belong to a funnel
units.content: Reach, engagement, clicks, leads, sales, retention, and margin answer different questions. A metric is useful only when tied to the stage and decision it represents.

units.title: Campaign measurement review
units.content: Record spend and effort; track reach and qualified traffic; measure lead rate, conversion rate, revenue, margin, and retention where available; compare against baseline; then decide what to stop, continue, or test next.

units.title: Analytics failures
units.content: Avoid celebrating reach when lead quality falls, treating correlation as causation, changing multiple variables at once without noting it, and ignoring creative or channel cost in return calculations.

drills.title: Diagnose a weak campaign
drills.prompt: A campaign has strong views, low clicks, average leads, and weak sales. Identify likely funnel problems and the next measurement or test needed.

competencies.name: Growth Experiments
competencies.description: Run bounded tests to improve acquisition, conversion, retention, or monetization.
competencies.purpose: Learn quickly without confusing random changes with evidence.

units.title: Growth experiment design
units.content: State hypothesis, target metric, audience, change, baseline, duration, guardrail metrics, and success threshold before launching; change as few variables as practical; document result and confidence.

units.title: Test the bottleneck, not the easiest thing to change
units.content: Improving a metric that is not limiting the business can create activity without meaningful growth. Find the current constraint first.

units.title: Experiment failures
units.content: Avoid declaring winners from tiny samples, stopping only when results look favorable, changing the offer and channel simultaneously, and running tests with no decision attached.

drills.title: Design a conversion experiment
drills.prompt: Design a test for a service booking page with traffic but weak inquiry conversion. Define hypothesis, one primary change, metric, guardrails, duration logic, and decision rule.
